html:
The Guajajara are an Indigenous people of the state of Maranhão in northeast Brazil, among the most numerous in the country. They call themselves Tenetehara and speak a Tupi-Guarani language shared with the Tembé of Pará.

They met French and Portuguese traders in the early 1600s, and Jesuits ran missions among them in the 1600s and 1700s. Their long contact did not end conflict: in 1901 a revolt at the Alto Alegre mission was crushed by force. Today their forest lands, such as Arariboia, are under pressure from illegal loggers, and Guajajara "Guardians of the Forest" patrol them; several have been killed. In 2023 Sônia Guajajara became Brazil's first Minister of Indigenous Peoples.
